title: Probabilistic alert scoring and suppression for usage/cost/latency pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our current pipeline emits many noisy notifications for short-lived usage/cost/latency excursions. This ticket implements a probabilistic scoring layer to score candidate events by likelihood-of-true-incident and suppress low-value noise. Goals: reduce alert volume to on-call and customers while preserving detection of real regressions and cost spikes; provide contextual evidence for each notification (correlated metrics, affected tenants, recent deploys) so triage is faster. Scope: server-side scoring service that consumes existing aggregated telemetry (per-tenant ingestion rates, token counts, p99 latency, cost accrual) from the usage ingestion topics; a suppression manager that enforces per-signal suppression policies and backoff; dashboard and runbook updates. This is a behavioral change to the alerts service, not the primary detector logic. Detector outputs remain upstream (z-scores/changepoints), but the scoring service decides whether and how to notify.
design_notes: Core idea: treat each candidate event E (time window W, metric M, tenant T) as generating evidence and compute P(true incident | E, context) using a lightweight Bayesian model plus heuristics. Inputs: historical baseline distribution for (T,M,W), recent trend features (slope, burstiness), cross-metric correlation signatures, deployment markers, and tenant risk score (past incident rate, SLA tier). Scoring pipeline: 1) feature enrich (lookup baselines, retrieve last 60m traces), 2) compute likelihood ratio for sudden shift vs normal variability, 3) apply tenant-adjusted prior -> posterior score in [0,1], 4) map posterior to actions: immediate-page (p>0.95), paging with enrichment (0.8-0.95), email/digest (0.4-0.8), suppress and log (<0.4). Suppression rules: sliding exponential backoff per (tenant, metric, route) with progressive decay; suppression windows respect SLA customers (min suppression for P0 customers). Additional components: grouping engine to collapse repeated events into a single notification when root cause signatures match; enrichment fetchers for correlated signals (cost, latency, errors) and recent deploys (from CI tags). Performance constraints: scoring must handle ~10k candidate events/sec at peak; target 50ms median decision latency; state lookups should be backed by Redis with cache warming for hot tenants. Privacy/compliance: do not include raw tenant payloads in external emails; audit logs required for all suppressed events. Implementation decisions: prefer logistic/Bayesian mixture model for interpretability; reserve ML heavy models to future phase after baseline metrics improve.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end scoring service exists and accepts candidate events from existing detector topic; 2) For a labeled testbench of 500 historical incidents and 1500 known-noise windows, precision at score >=0.8 >= 92% and false positive rate reduced by >=40% vs current rule-based routing; 3) Suppression manager applies backoff rules and provides per-tenant suppression state visible in console; 4) Notifications include contextual blocks: top 3 correlated metrics, recent deploy id, tenant risk tag, and a link to the relevant dashboard; 5) Canary rollout to 5% of tenants for 7 days with monitoring verifying no missed P0 incidents; 6) Audit log entries for every suppressed event are written to long-term store for 90 days; 7) Runbook updated with kill-switch instructions and telemetry to revert to old behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy scoring service to staging and route 5% of low-risk tenants' alerts for 7 days; monitor precision/recall proxies, notification latency, and on-call noise metrics. Phase 2 (expand): 20% for 72 hours, include medium-risk tenants. Phase 3 (opt-in): beta customers (5 customers) opt into suppression + enriched notifications. Phase 4 (global): enable by default with opt-out and tiered suppression thresholds. Rollback plan: feature-flag controlled; immediate rollback flips to 'always notify' path. Key gating metrics: missed-P0 count (must be zero), mean notifications per tenant/day (-40% target), median time-to-notify < previous baseline + 100ms. Communication: pre-flight email to success and affected customers, internal postmortem template prepared.
monitoring_and_metrics: Dashboards to create: 'Scoring Health' with histogram of posterior scores, top suppressed tenants, suppression window distribution, decision-latency P50/P95, and feature fetch errors. Alerting: create internal alert if decision latency P95 > 500ms or cache miss rate > 5% for 15m. KPIs: false-positive-rate estimate, notifications-per-tenant-day, percentage of candidate events suppressed, missed-P0 incidents. Logging: human-readable audit entry for suppressed events stored in S3 with tenant id, metric, timestamp, score, and suppression reason. Post-deploy experiments: A/B cohort to measure downstream customer support tickets reduction and mean time to acknowledge incidents.
implementation_tasks: Prototype scoring function + offline evaluation on labeled dataset
Implement enrichment layer (deploy lookup + correlated metric fetch) with caching
Build scoring microservice (k8s) with Redis backed state store
Create suppression manager with per-tenant exponential backoff state and admin API
Integrate with notification router (Slack/email/pagerduty) via feature flag
Add audit-log writer and S3 lifecycle policy
Console UI: show suppressed events and allow manual release
Create runbook and internal docs; schedule on-call walkthrough
